claim: The Spindle Assembly Checkpoint (SAC) is a conserved signaling pathway that delays anaphase onset until all chromosomes are attached to spindle microtubules.
source: Faithfull genome partitioning during cell division relies on the Spindle Assembly Checkpoint (SAC), a conserved signaling pathway that delays anaphase onset until all chromosomes are attached to spindle microtubules.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in cell biology supported by extensive literature and is stated as background knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Mps1 kinase is an upstream SAC regulator that promotes the assembly of an anaphase inhibitor through a sequential multi-target phosphorylation cascade.
source: Mps1 kinase is an upstream SAC regulator that promotes the assembly of an anaphase inhibitor through a sequential multi-target phosphorylation cascade.
evidence: This statement is supported by established scientific knowledge about Mps1's role in SAC signaling.

claim: Mps1 activity peaks in early mitosis as a result of its T-loop autophosphorylation.
source: Thus, the SAC is highly responsive to Mps1, whose activity peaks in early mitosis as a result of its T-loop autophosphorylation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about Mps1 regulation.

claim: The mechanism controlling Mps1 inactivation once kinetochores attach to microtubules and the SAC is satisfied remains unknown.
source: However, the mechanism controlling Mps1 inactivation once kinetochores attach to microtubules and the SAC is satisfied remains unknown.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in knowledge that the study aims to address.

claim: Protein Phosphatase 1 (PP1) inactivates Mps1 by dephosphorylating its T-loop in vitro and in Drosophila.
source: Here we show in vitro and in Drosophila that Protein Phosphatase 1 (PP1) inactivates Mps1 by dephosphorylating its T-loop.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: PP1-mediated dephosphorylation of Mps1 occurs at kinetochores and in the cytosol.
source: PP1-mediated dephosphorylation of Mps1 occurs at kinetochores and in the cytosol, and inactivation of both pools of Mps1 during metaphase is essential to ensure prompt and efficient SAC silencing.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Inactivation of both kinetochore and cytosolic pools of Mps1 during metaphase is essential to ensure prompt and efficient SAC silencing.
source: PP1-mediated dephosphorylation of Mps1 occurs at kinetochores and in the cytosol, and inactivation of both pools of Mps1 during metaphase is essential to ensure prompt and efficient SAC silencing.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Depletion of PP1-87B from Drosophila S2 cells results in an abnormal accumulation of Mad1 at aligned kinetochores.
source: Live cell-imaging analysis showed that depletion of PP1-87B orthologue from Drosophila S2 cells results in an abnormal accumulation of Mad1 at aligned kinetochores and a pronounced extension of the metaphase duration (Figure 1A,B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Videos 1 and 2).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 1A,B.

claim: Depletion of PP1-87B from Drosophila S2 cells results in a pronounced extension of the metaphase duration.
source: Live cell-imaging analysis showed that depletion of PP1-87B orthologue from Drosophila S2 cells results in an abnormal accumulation of Mad1 at aligned kinetochores and a pronounced extension of the metaphase duration (Figure 1A,B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Videos 1 and 2).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 1A,B.

claim: Co-depletion of Mps1 prevented the anaphase onset delay caused by PP1-87B depletion, indicating it is due to active SAC signaling.
source: Co-depletion of Mps1 prevented the anaphase onset delay, indicating it is due to active SAC signaling (Figure 1A,B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Video 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that Mps1 depletion rescues the PP1-87B depletion phenotype.

claim: Depletion of PP1-87B from Drosophila S2 cells increased Aurora B activation at centromeres/kinetochores of prometaphase and metaphase chromosomes.
source: We found that depletion of PP1-87B from Drosophila S2 cells increased Aurora B activation at centromeres/kinetochores of prometaphase and metaphase chromosomes, as expected (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: The inter-kinetochore distances on aligned chromosomes in PP1-87B depleted cells were similar to those measured in control cells.
source: However, the inter-kinetochore distances on aligned chromosomes were similar to those measured in control cells (Figure 1E), indicating that kinetochores are under mechanical tension compatible with stably attached microtubules (Li and Nicklas, 1995; Akiyoshi et al., 2010; Khodjakov and Pines, 2010; Ye et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1E and cited literature.

claim: PP1-87B depleted cells revealed the presence of cold stable kinetochore-fibers, as observed in control cells.
source: In agreement, PP1-87B depleted cells revealed the presence of cold stable kinetochore-fibers, as observed in control cells (Figure 1F,G).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1F,G.

claim: Depletion of PP1-87B fails to cause significant changes in the stability of kinetochore-microtubule attachments in metaphase cells.
source: Depletion of PP1-87B fails to cause significant changes in the stability of kinetochore-microtubule attachments in metaphase cells and there are no significant differences in the fractions of microtubules in the stable (KT-MT) versus unstable (non-KT-MT) populations when compared to control cells (Figure 1H,I; Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Videos 4 and 5).
evidence: This is supported by inducible speckle imaging data shown in Figure 1H,I.

claim: Mad1 accumulation at metaphase-aligned kinetochores and the delayed anaphase onset observed in PP1-87B-depleted cells are not caused by unattached kinetochores transiently generated as a result of increased Aurora B activity.
source: Taken together, these results clearly show that Mad1 accumulation at metaphase-aligned kinetochores and the delayed anaphase onset observed in PP1-87B-depleted cells are not caused by unattached kinetochores transiently generated as a result of increased Aurora B activity.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the combined data showing stable attachments despite increased Aurora B activity.

claim: Depletion of PP1-87B has no significant impact on Mps1 kinetochore localization.
source: Immunofluorescence analysis showed that depletion of PP1-87B has no significant impact on Mps1 kinetochore localization.
evidence: This is stated as a result from immunofluorescence analysis.

claim: Mps1 accumulates at prometaphase kinetochores and its levels decrease significantly as microtubules attach, with a fraction of Mps1 persisting at kinetochores of metaphase chromosomes.
source: Mps1 accumulates at prometaphase kinetochores and its levels decrease significantly as microtubules attach, with a fraction of Mps1 persisting at kinetochores of metaphase chromosomes (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A-D.

claim: The residual pool of Mps1 is retained at bioriented kinetochores until anaphase onset, even after establishment of inter-kinetochore tension.
source: This residual pool of Mps1 is retained at bioriented kinetochores until anaphase onset, even after establishment of inter-kinetochore tension, as revealed by live imaging of S2 cells expressing EGFP-Mps1 under control of Mps1 cis-regulatory region (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B and Video 6).
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Depletion of PP1-87B resulted in a substantial increase of Mps1 T-loop autophosphorylation during prometaphase and on metaphases kinetochores stably attached to microtubule bundles.
source: Interestingly, we found that depletion of PP1-87B resulted in a substantial increase of Mps1 T-loop autophosphorylation during prometaphase and on metaphases kinetochores stably attached to microtubule bundles (Figure 2A–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–F with phospho-antibody characterization described in supplementary information).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data using phospho-specific antibody shown in Figure 2A-D.

claim: Depletion of PP1 noncatalytic subunit Sds22/PPP1R7 mimicked PP1-87B RNAi by increasing Mps1 T490 phosphorylation both at unattached and aligned kinetochores.
source: Moreover, depletion of PP1 noncatalytic subunit Sds22/PPP1R7, which positively regulates the phosphatase activity at kinetochores (Posch et al., 2010; Wurzenberger et al., 2012; Heroes et al., 2013), mimicked PP1-87B RNAi by increasing Mps1 T490 phosphorylation both at unattached and aligned kinetochores (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A-D and cited literature.

claim: Drosophila Mps1 exhibits a fast turnover rate at unattached kinetochores that relies in part on its kinase activity.
source: Drosophila Mps1 exhibits a fast turnover rate at unattached kinetochores that relies in part on its kinase activity, as revealed by FRAP measurements of wild type (WT) and kinase-dead (KD) versions of EGFP-Mps1 expressed in S2 cells (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: This is supported by FRAP data shown in Figure 2E,F.

claim: Both the half-life and stable population of Mps1 increase at metaphase kinetochores.
source: In line with the observed reduction in Mps1 T490 autophosphorylation, both the half-life and stable population of Mps1 increase at metaphase kinetochores (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: This is supported by FRAP data shown in Figure 2E,F.

claim: In the absence of PP1-87B, Mps1 displays a faster dynamic exchange at aligned kinetochores.
source: However, in the absence of PP1-87B, Mps1 displays a faster dynamic exchange at aligned kinetochores, as expected from enhanced kinase activity (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: This is supported by FRAP data shown in Figure 2E,F and is consistent with enhanced kinase activity.

claim: PP1-87B activity is required to repress the activating autophosphorylation of Mps1 that remains associated with metaphase kinetochores.
source: Collectively, these results demonstrate that PP1-87B activity is required to represses the activating autophosphorylation of Mps1 that remains associated with metaphase kinetochores.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data.

claim: Simultaneous incubation of PP1-γ with recombinant versions of human (Mps1/TTK) and Drosophila Mps1 orthologues led to a concentration-dependent decrease of T676 and T490 autophosphorylation, respectively.
source: Simultaneous incubation of PP1-γ with recombinant versions of human (Mps1/TTK) and Drosophila Mps1 orthologues led to a concentration-dependent decrease of T676 (T676Ph) and T490 (T490Ph) autophosphorylation, respectively (Figure 3A,C).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro kinase/phosphatase assay data shown in Figure 3A,C.

claim: PP1-γ was able to dephosphorylate the T-loop of Mps1/TTK that had been previously activated by autophosphorylation.
source: Moreover, PP1-γ was able to dephosphorylate the T-loop of Mps1/TTK that had been previously activated by autophosphorylation (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro phosphatase assay data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: λ-phosphatase failed to antagonize to the same extent the autophosphorylation of human Mps1/TTK T676 and of Drosophila Mps1 T490.
source: In contrast, λ-phosphatase failed to antagonize to the same extent the autophosphorylation of human Mps1/TTK T676 and of Drosophila Mps1 T490 (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1), indicating a higher specificity of PP1-γ towards Mps1 T-loop in vitro.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro phosphatase assay data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Drosophila Mps1 N-terminus contains a clear match for a PP1-docking motif of the [R/K]VxF – type.
source: Drosophila Mps1 N-terminus contains a clear match for a PP1-docking motif of the [R/K]VxF – type (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: EGFP-Mps1WT from S2 cell lysates bound efficiently to recombinant MBP-PP1-87B but not to the MBP used as negative control.
source: The interaction between Mps1 and PP1-87B was confirmed in pull-down assays in which EGFP-Mps1WT from S2 cell lysates bound efficiently to recombinant MBP-PP1-87B but not to the MBP used as negative control (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by pull-down assay data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Mutating Mps1 KVLF231-234 to AVLA231-234 markedly decreased the ability of EGFP-Mps1 to interact with MBP-PP1-87B.
source: Conversely, mutating Mps1 KVLF231-234 to AVLA231-234 markedly decreased the ability of EGFP-Mps1 to interact with MBP-PP1-87B, hence validating KVLF as a PP1-binding motif (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: This is supported by pull-down assay data shown in Figure 3E,F.

claim: 6xHis-N-Mps1WT bound efficiently to MBP-PP1-87B, while the fragment 6xHis-N-Mps1K231A/F234A did not.
source: While 6xHis-N-Mps1WT bound efficiently to MBP-PP1-87B, the fragment 6xHis-N-Mps1K231A/F234A did not (Figure 3G), thus confirming that the KVLF motif mediates a direct interaction between Mps1 N-terminus and PP1-87B.
evidence: This is supported by pull-down assay data with purified recombinant proteins shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Recombinant PP1-γ antagonized with discernible less efficiency the T-loop autophosphorylation of EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A in comparison to EGFP-Mps1WT.
source: In accordance, in vitro assays with EGFP-Mps1 immunoprecipitated from mitotic S2 cell lysates showed that recombinant PP1-γ antagonized with discernible less efficiency the T-loop autophosphorylation of EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A in comparison to EGFP-Mps1WT (Figure 3H,I).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro dephosphorylation assay data shown in Figure 3H,I.

claim: Mps1 T-loop is a direct substrate of PP1-87B/PP1-γ.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that Mps1 T-loop is a direct substrate of PP1-87B/PP1-γ.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the combined in vitro and cellular data.

claim: MBP-PP1-87B failed to pull-down EGFP-Mps1WT from S2 cells depleted of Sds22/PPP1R7.
source: However, we found that MBP-PP1-87B failed to pull-down EGFP-Mps1WT from S2 cells depleted of Sds22/PPP1R7 (Figure 3E,F), which suggests that in addition to the KVLF motif on the kinase N-terminus, the Sds22/PPP1R7 regulatory subunit is also required for competent binding of full-length Mps1 to PP1-87B in cell extracts.
evidence: This is supported by pull-down assay data shown in Figure 3E,F.

claim: Phosphorylation of T490 at unaligned kinetochores was significantly higher for EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A relative to EGFP-Mps1WT.
source: Phosphorylation of T490 at unaligned kinetochores was significantly higher for EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A relative to EGFP-Mps1WT (Figure 3J,L).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3J,L.

claim: A similar increment in the T-loop activation status was observed for EGFP-Mps1WT of prometaphase cells depleted of PP1-87B.
source: A similar increment in the T-loop activation status was observed for EGFP-Mps1WT of prometaphase cells depleted of PP1-87B (Figure 3J,L).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3J,L.

claim: The mutation KVLF231-234 prevented the dephosphorylation of Mps1 T-loop also at bioriented kinetochores.
source: Notably, the mutation KVLF231-234 prevented the dephosphorylation of Mps1 T-loop also at bioriented kinetochores, mimicking the result obtained in metaphase cells expressing EGFP-Mps1WT in the absence of PP1-87B (Figure 3K,L).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3K,L.

claim: EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A exhibits faster dynamics than EGFP-Mps1WT at aligned kinetochores.
source: As expected from increased T490 autophosphorylation, EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A exhibits faster dynamics than EGFP-Mps1WT at aligned kinetochores (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by FRAP data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A,B.

claim: PP1-87B directly controls Mps1 T-loop dephosphorylation at kinetochores during prometaphase and metaphase.
source: From these results, we conclude that PP1-87B directly controls Mps1 T-loop dephosphorylation at kinetochores during prometaphase and metaphase.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data.

claim: Expression of EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A caused a pronounced metaphase delay when compared to EGFP-Mps1WT expressing cells.
source: Live-cell imaging revealed that expression of EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A caused a pronounced metaphase delay when compared to EGFP-Mps1WT expressing cells (Figure 4A,B; Videos 7 and 8).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: Depletion of BubR1 prevented the metaphase delay caused by EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A expression, showing it is SAC-dependent.
source: Depletion of BubR1 prevented this delay showing it is SAC-dependent (Figure 4A,B and Video 9).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: The inter-kinetochore distances monitored throughout metaphase and the attachments of bioriented kinetochores to cold-resistant microtubule bundles in EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A cells were similar to those observed in metaphase cells expressing the wild-type kinase.
source: However, the delay is not caused by unstable kinetochore-microtubule interactions, since the inter-kinetochore distances monitored throughout metaphase and the attachments of bioriented kinetochores to cold-resistant microtubule bundles in EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A cells were similar to those observed in metaphase cells expressing the wild-type kinase (Figure 4C,D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4C,D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Cells expressing EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A retained higher levels of Mad1 at aligned kinetochores.
source: Nevertheless, cells expressing EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A retained higher levels of Mad1 at aligned kinetochores (Figure 4E,F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B,C), which is consistent with lasting Mps1 activation and SAC signaling in metaphase.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4E,F.

claim: Impairing PP1-mediated dephosphorylation of the residual pool of Mps1 that remains associated with kinetochores of bioriented chromosomes is sufficient to delay SAC silencing and prevent anaphase onset despite normal chromosome attachment and high inter-kinetochore tension.
source: These results strongly suggest that impairing PP1-mediated dephosphorylation of the residual pool of Mps1 that remains associated with kinetochores of bioriented chromosomes is sufficient to delay SAC silencing and prevent anaphase onset despite normal chromosome attachment and high inter-kinetochore tension.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data.

claim: Expression of EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A partially rescued Mps1 T490 phosphorylation, Mad1 kinetochore recruitment and consistently attenuated the decline of SAC function following Aurora B inhibition.
source: Strikingly, expression of EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A partially rescued Mps1 T490 phosphorylation, Mad1 kinetochore recruitment and consistently attenuated the decline of SAC function following Aurora B inhibition (Figure 4G–I).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence and mitotic index data shown in Figure 4G-I.

claim: Compromising Mps1 T-loop dephosphorylation is sufficient to delay SAC silencing and mitotic exit.
source: Collectively, these results demonstrate that compromising Mps1 T-loop dephosphorylation is sufficient to delay SAC silencing and mitotic exit.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data.

claim: PP1-mediated dephosphorylation of Mps1 T-loop is required for efficient Mps1 inactivation and consequently for prompt SAC silencing.
source: Thus, we conclude that PP1-mediated dephosphorylation of Mps1 T-loop is required for efficient Mps1 inactivation and consequently for prompt SAC silencing.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data.

claim: Mps1 T-loop activation is first detected in the nucleoplasm and on pre-kinetochores during prophase.
source: Mps1 T-loop activation is first detected in the nucleoplasm and on pre-kinetochores during prophase (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Kinetochore-null S2 cells engendered through CENP-C knockdown retain high levels of nucleoplasmic Mps1 T490 phosphorylation.
source: Interestingly, kinetochore-null S2 cells engendered through CENP-C knockdown retain high levels of nucleoplasmic Mps1 T490 phosphorylation (Figure 5A,B), indicating that Mps1 activation at mitotic entry can occur through kinetochore-independent mechanisms.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: In the absence of kinetochores, cells expressing EGFP-Mps1WT rapidly progressed through mitosis, whereas expression of EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A markedly delayed anaphase onset.
source: Live-cell imaging revealed that in the absence of kinetochores, cells expressing EGFP-Mps1WT rapidly progressed through mitosis, whereas expression of EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A markedly delayed anaphase onset (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: Preventing MCC assembly through BubR1 co-depletion or expressing Mps1K231A/F234A harboring unphosphorylatable T490 (EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A/T490A), failed to cause an obvious increase in the mitotic timing.
source: Importantly, preventing MCC assembly through BubR1 co-depletion or expressing Mps1K231A/F234A harboring unphosphorylatable T490 (EGFP-Mps1K231A/F234A/T490A), failed to cause an obvious increase in the mitotic timing indicating that the delay in mitosis observed in kinetochore-null Mps1K231A/F234A cells is SAC-dependent and requires Mps1 activating T-loop autophosphorylation (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: Impairing T-loop dephosphorylation of cytosolic Mps1 prolongs mitosis in a SAC-dependent manner even in the absence of a kinetochore-generated 'wait anaphase' signal.
source: These results show that impairing T-loop dephosphorylation of cytosolic Mps1 prolongs mitosis in a SAC-dependent manner even in the absence of a kinetochore-generated 'wait anaphase' signal.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the kinetochore-null cell experiments.

claim: Timely transition to anaphase requires that SAC extinction at stably attached kinetochores coincides with the inactivation of cytosolic Mps1.
source: Therefore, timely transition to anaphase requires that SAC extinction at stably attached kinetochores coincides with the inactivation of cytosolic Mps1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data.

claim: PP1-mediated dephosphorylation of non-kinetochore Mps1 is a critical mechanism to efficiently silence the SAC and ensure prompt anaphase onset.
source: These results allow us to conclude that PP1-mediated dephosphorylation of non-kinetochore Mps1 is a critical mechanism to efficiently silence the SAC and ensure prompt anaphase onset.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study.

claim: PP1-87B preferentially accumulates on kinetochores when chromosomes are bioriented at the metaphase plate.
source: Immunofluorescence analysis of S2 cells revealed that PP1-87B preferentially accumulates on kinetochores when chromosomes are bioriented at the metaphase plate (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: Inhibition of Aurora B led to an increase of PP1-87B levels at unattached kinetochores.
source: Inhibition of Aurora B led to an increase of PP1-87B levels at unattached kinetochores (Figure 6C,D), suggesting that similarly to the described for human cells, Aurora B activity limits the association of PP1-87B with unattached/unaligned kinetochores in flies.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6C,D.

claim: Inhibition of CDK1 with RO-3306 in colchicine-treated S2 cells led to a reduction of Mps1 T490 autophosphorylation at unattached kinetochores, which was partially restored upon depletion of PP1-87B.
source: In accordance, inhibition of CDK1 with RO-3306 in colchicine-treated S2 cells led to a reduction of Mps1 T490 autophosphorylation at unattached kinetochores, which was partially restored upon depletion of PP1-87B (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6E,F.

claim: CDK1-dependent inhibition of PP1-87B contributes to maintain Mps1 active in prometaphase S2 cells.
source: Thus, although CDK1 might also directly potentiate Mps1 activity (Morin et al., 2012), these results suggest that CDK1-dependent inhibition of PP1-87B contributes to maintain Mps1 active in prometaphase S2 cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the CDK1 inhibition experiments and cited literature.

claim: Cyclin B starts to be rapidly degraded upon biorientation of all chromosomes.
source: We monitored by live-cell imaging the levels of EGFP-Cyclin B throughout mitosis in S2 cells and as expected found that it starts to be rapidly degraded upon biorientation of all chromosomes (Figure 6G,H and Video 14).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 6G,H.

claim: Proteolysis of Cyclin B also occurs during prometaphase but at a significant lower rate.
source: Interestingly, we could further observe that proteolysis of Cyclin B also occurs during prometaphase but at a significant lower rate (Figure 6G,H and Video 14).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 6G,H.

claim: The modest decline in Cyclin B that takes place before metaphase might be critical to permit PP1-mediated inactivation of Mps1 and SAC silencing.
source: Thus, the modest decline in Cyclin B that takes place before metaphase might be critical to permit PP1-mediated inactivation of Mps1 and SAC silencing.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed Cyclin B degradation pattern and cited literature.

claim: Mps1 orthologues encompass several other PP1-binding motifs within different regions of the kinase, such as SILK signatures in the C-terminus of human and mouse Mps1.
source: Importantly, Mps1 orthologues encompass several other PP1-binding motifs within different regions of the kinase, such as SILK signatures in the C-terminus of human and mouse Mps1.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from sequence analysis.

claim: Despite the diversification in type and localization of PP1-docking motifs among Mps1 orthologues, the dephosphorylation of the kinase T-loop by PP1 is likely to be conserved.
source: This suggests that despite the diversification in type and localization of PP1-docking motifs among Mps1 orthologues, the dephosphorylation of the kinase T-loop by PP1 is likely to be conserved.
evidence: This is an inference based on the presence of PP1-binding motifs in different Mps1 orthologues.

claim: Microtubules forming end-on attachments outcompete Mps1 for Ndc80 binding.
source: Because microtubules bind to the same surface of the CH domains that interacts with Mps1, microtubules forming end-on attachments outcompete Mps1 for Ndc80 binding (Hiruma et al., 2015; Ji et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by cited literature.

claim: The competition mechanism between microtubules and Mps1 for Ndc80 binding is consistent with the reduction of Mps1 from metaphase kinetochores, but is however insufficient to dislodge all Mps1 molecules.
source: This competition mechanism is consistent with the reduction of Mps1 from metaphase kinetochores, but is however insufficient to dislodge all Mps1 molecules.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of existing knowledge.

claim: Drosophila kinetochores retain a fraction of Mps1 even after the formation of end-on attachments that exert proper kinetochore tension.
source: As in human and budding yeast (Vázquez-Novelle and Petronczki, 2010; Aravamudhan et al., 2015), Drosophila kinetochores retain a fraction of Mps1 even after the formation of end-on attachments that exert proper kinetochore tension.
evidence: This is stated as an observation consistent with findings in other organisms, supported by citations.

claim: Low levels of Mps1 were shown to be sufficient to delay anaphase onset.
source: Intriguingly, although low levels of Mps1 were shown to be sufficient to delay anaphase onset (Herriott et al., 2012; Foijer et al., 2014), the residual pool of Mps1 at metaphase kinetochores does not prevent SAC silencing.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by cited literature.

claim: In Drosophila and in human cells, an Spc105/KNL1- and Bub1-independent pathway also recruits Mad1-Mad2 to unattached kinetochores.
source: In Drosophila and in human cells however, an Spc105/KNL1- and Bub1-independent pathway also recruits Mad1-Mad2 to unattached kinetochores (Schittenhelm et al., 2009; Caldas et al., 2015; Silió et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by cited literature.

claim: The recruitment of Mad1-Mad2 through the RZZ complex relies on the localization of the RZZ complex at kinetochores, which is itself regulated by Mps1 activity.
source: This relies on the localization of the RZZ complex at kinetochores, which is itself regulated by Mps1 activity (Santaguida et al., 2010) and is sufficient to activate the SAC in response to unattached kinetochores, even in the absence of KNL1 (Schittenhelm et al., 2009; Silió et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by cited literature.

claim: Intra-kinetochore tension or alterations on kinetochore architecture are important not only to disrupt the interaction of Mps1 with its kinetochore substrates but also to increase the recruitment of PP1 to metaphase chromosomes.
source: Thus, we reason that intra-kinetochore tension or alterations on kinetochore architecture, which also correlate with SAC satisfaction in Drosophila and human cells (Maresca and Salmon, 2009; Uchida et al., 2009), are important not only to disrupt the interaction of Mps1 with its kinetochore substrates but also to increase the recruitment of PP1 to metaphase chromosomes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined data and cited literature.

claim: Kinetochore levels of PP1-87B in Drosophila S2 cells are significantly higher at bioriented chromosomes.
source: Similarly to human cells (Liu et al., 2010), kinetochore levels of PP1-87B in Drosophila S2 cells are significantly higher at bioriented chromosomes.
evidence: This is stated as an observation consistent with findings in human cells, supported by citation.

claim: At tensionless kinetochores, the recruitment of PP1-γ is limited due to phosphorylation of Spc105/KNL1 N-terminus and of the Ska complex by Aurora B.
source: At tensionless kinetochores, the recruitment of PP1-γ is limited due to phosphorylation of Spc105/KNL1 N-terminus and of the Ska complex by Aurora B, which respectively inhibits the binding of PP1-γ to Spc105/KNL1 and Ska kinetochore localization (Liu et al., 2010; Chan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by cited literature.

claim: As microtubules bind to kinetochores and tension is established, the spatial repositioning of the KMN network decreases Aurora-B mediated phosphorylation of the Ska complex and of Spc105/KNL1 N-terminus.
source: As microtubules bind to kinetochores and tension is established, the spatial repositioning of the KMN network decreases Aurora-B mediated phosphorylation of the Ska complex and of Spc105/KNL1 N-terminus (Welburn et al., 2010), hence allowing bulk accumulation of PP1-γ, which then catalyses the dephosphorylation of Mps1 T-loop.
evidence: This is stated as a mechanism based on established knowledge and cited literature.

claim: Inhibition of Mps1 causes a substantial decrease in pre-mitotic MCC levels and a consequent reduction in Cyclin B levels already in G2 and prophase.
source: Interestingly, inhibition of Mps1 causes a substantial decrease in pre-mitotic MCC levels and a consequent reduction in Cyclin B levels already in G2 and prophase (Maciejowski et al., 2010; Rodriguez-Bravo et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by cited literature.

claim: A truncated form of Mps1 unable to localize at kinetochores failed to promote the recruitment of Bub1 to unattached kinetochores but was nevertheless sufficient to sustain the assembly of mitotic APC/C inhibitory complexes and delay anaphase onset.
source: Moreover, a truncated form of Mps1 unable to localize at kinetochores failed to promote the recruitment of Bub1 to unattached kinetochores but was nevertheless sufficient to sustain the assembly of mitotic APC/C inhibitory complexes and delay anaphase onset (Maciejowski et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by cited literature.

claim: Cytosolic Mps1 activity was shown to be critical to maintain the metaphase arrest caused by Mad1 constitutively tethered to stably attached bioriented kinetochores that were stripped from Mps1.
source: In addition, cytosolic Mps1 activity was shown to be critical to maintain the metaphase arrest caused by Mad1 constitutively tethered to stably attached bioriented kinetochores that were stripped from Mps1 (Maldonado and Kapoor, 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by cited literature.

claim: Kinetochore recruitment of Mps1 substantially increases the cell capacity to sustain a prolonged mitotic arrest when challenged with spindle poisons.
source: Although kinetochore recruitment of Mps1 substantially increases the cell capacity to sustain a prolonged mitotic arrest when challenged with spindle poisons (Nijenhuis et al., 2013), during an unperturbed mitosis in which MCC production at kinetochores is minimal (Collin et al., 2013; Dick and Gerlich, 2013), controlled activity of soluble Mps1 is expected to be particularly relevant.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by cited literature.

claim: CDK1 phosphorylation of PP1 C-terminus represses the phosphatase activity during early mitosis.
source: CDK1 phosphorylation of PP1 C-terminus represses the phosphatase activity during early mitosis (Dohadwala et al., 1994; Yamano et al., 1994; Wu et al., 2009; Grallert et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by cited literature.

claim: The SAC is switched off under condition of high CDK1/Cyclin B activity.
source: However, several lines of evidence indicate that the SAC is switched off under condition of high CDK1/Cyclin B activity (Mirchenko and Uhlmann, 2010; Oliveira et al., 2010; Kamenz and Hauf, 2014; Rattani et al., 2014; Vázquez-Novelle et al., 2014), hence challenging the impact that CDK1/Cyclin B-mediated regulation of PP1 might have on SAC silencing.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by cited literature.

claim: Small decreases in CDK1/Cyclin B activity are sufficient to initiate PP1 re-activation of and trigger a positive feedback loop that ensures robust phosphatase activity.
source: Interestingly, recent mathematical modelling support that small decreases in CDK1/Cyclin B activity are sufficient to initiate PP1 re-activation of and trigger a positive feedback loop that ensures robust phosphatase activity (Rogers et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by cited literature.

claim: Cyclin A is progressively degraded during prometaphase and its abundance governs the overall stability of kinetochore-microtubule attachments, which increases in metaphase when cyclin A levels fall below a critical threshold.
source: Cyclin A is progressively degraded during prometaphase and its abundance governs the overall stability of kinetochore-microtubule attachments, which increases in metaphase when cyclin A levels fall below a critical threshold (Kabeche and Compton, 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by cited literature.
